articles.title: 'People call them pervert glasses but they give me independence'
articles.summary: Concerns about the use of smart glasses are having an affect on visually-impaired users.
articles.body:
Fraser Fleming approaches the corner of a busy Glasgow city centre street and asks his smart glasses to describe the road ahead.

A voice coming from tiny speakers in the arms of the specs tells him there are several parked cars and a person walking in his direction.

For 44-year-old Fraser, who is registered blind, this is "game changing" information.

"I know how to approach the street and what sort of care to take," he says.

"If I need to maybe take my time or if I can just walk at normal pace."

Fraser, who began losing his sight in his early twenties, says his AI-powered Meta smart glasses have become part of his everyday life during the past two years.

They help him to navigate public transport, read street signs and order from menus – but he's started to think twice about wearing them in public.

"People are calling them pervert glasses," he says, referring to multiple reports of them being used to secretly film and harass people, particularly women and girls , with the footage being shared online.

Fraser says this is having a negative effect on anyone wearing them, including visually-impaired people.

"We are definitely not using them to record people in dodgy situations," he says.

"We're using them to lead an independent life."

They were labelled 'pervert glasses'. Will a camera-free version transform their image?

The Meta glasses revolution - is it okay to film people in public?

TikToker faces police probe over secret filming using 'smart glasses'

Fraser, from Motherwell, told the BBC's Your Voice he would often take his glasses off if he thought there was a chance of a confrontation.

"I've got enough to worry about getting from A to B," he says.

"I'll just put the glasses away and have to rely on my other senses in order to navigate around, which is going to make life a lot more difficult for me."

Tracey Rogerson, who uses the technology to help with her sight loss, shares Fraser's concerns.

"I was shocked to hear that they were being called pervert glasses because for me, they're such a big part of my life to help me maintain my independence," she says.

Meta, the company that owns WhatsApp, Facebook and Instagram, started selling smart glasses in 2021, and has sold about two million pairs since February last year.

It says there is a light on the frames which makes it clear the smart glasses are recording, but it also warns users not to engage in harmful activities.

As a result of the backlash against the glasses, some venues and events have banned or at least restricted their use over fears about covert filming, including ComicCon Scotland, which takes place in Edinburgh later this month.

This means Gordon Brown, who is severely sight-impaired and has attended the event with his family for the past three years, won't be going this year.

He says the impact of the ban on people with disabilities has been overlooked.

"Even if I was to put my glasses on quickly, just to read a sign or something, I wouldn't feel comfortable," says Gordon, from Inverkip.

"I think it's a matter of principle now, the fact that they're not willing to engage, and they're not willing to listen to a minority group.

"You know, we're not talking about thousands of people all of a sudden turning up wearing smart glasses."

Monopoly Events, which runs some of the biggest comic and entertainment conventions in the UK, announced in July that it had banned Meta glasses to "stop secret filming" of guests and attendees .

The ban applies to Meta glasses and other "wearable recording devices."

The company was contacted by the BBC about Gordon's comments.

Cosplay artist and performer Teah Pearn was at a comic convention in Birmingham earlier this year when she was secretly filmed.

She later discovered the footage was posted online.

Teah, who performs as Spill The Tea and has 1.9 million followers on TikTok, says she felt "violated".

"He was purposefully trying to provoke me or purposefully trying to make strange comments to get a reaction out of me so that he could get that perfect clip that he could post on social media and capitalise off it," says the London-based artist.

Teah says her experience demonstrates why restrictions are needed, but she thinks there should be exceptions for people with disabilities.

"For people who need the glasses and who really have to use them, I think they should be able to use them," she says.

"They shouldn't have to deal with the fact there's been a certain group of people who have spoiled it for them."

In a statement, Meta said: "We are proud that our AI glasses give blind, low-vision and hearing-impaired people greater independence in daily life.

"They were built to be noticed, which is why every pair with a camera has a bright light on the front that blinks when you take a photo or video.

"It cannot be turned off and the camera is disabled if someone covers or tampers with it."

articles.title: Washington captures record 2.16 million invasive green crabs in 2025-26; first detected in 2016, the species threatens marine life despite $8 million in funding, with no populations eradicated
articles.summary: Washington state removed more than 2.16 million invasive European green crabs from its marine waters during the 2026 fiscal year, marking a major effort
articles.body: Washington state removed more than 2.16 million invasive European green crabs from its marine waters during the 2026 fiscal year, marking a major effort to control a species threatening coastal ecosystems. According to the Washington Department of Fish and Wildlife (WDFW), the crabs were captured between July 1, 2025, and June 30, 2026. Despite the record catch, researchers warn that established populations have not been eradicated and the invasion could continue to worsen, putting native marine life at risk.The WDFW report said the Coastal Branch accounted for 2,133,725 of the captured crabs, while the Salish Sea Branch removed another 24,827 during the fiscal year.Green crab catches reached record highs in multiple months during the period. The department said the increase could be linked to greater funding for capture efforts, weather changes and continued growth in established populations.Despite the scale of the removal campaign, Washington has yet to eradicate any of its established invasive green crab populations.The department estimated that removing more than two million crabs may have prevented tens to hundreds of billions of green crab larvae from being released into state waters, potentially limiting further spread.Researchers warn invasive crab population remains a concernThe growing numbers have raised concerns among researchers monitoring the species. In 2022, former Washington Governor Jay Inslee declared an emergency over the invasive green crab population, after which the state legislature allocated more than $8 million to address the problem.Researcher Brian Turner acknowledged the scale of the increase, telling KUOW that officials had “seen some pretty dramatic increases”.“It's not good news,” he said.Researcher Emily Grason also warned that the invasion remains ongoing and could become more severe.“It's not hard to imagine the numbers could become worse. We are still in the middle of an ongoing invasion that hasn't necessarily reached any sort of equilibrium,” she said.How invasive green crabs threaten marine ecosystemsEuropean green crabs are considered an invasive species because they can disrupt ecosystems where they become established. According to the Washington Sea Grant Crab Team, the crabs can be accidentally transported to new habitats through marine vessels and seafood distribution.The first green crab was captured in Washington in 2016. The species is also invasive in places such as South Africa and Australia.Green crabs prey on clams, oysters, mussels, marine worms and small crustaceans. In environments where they have few natural predators, their feeding habits can put native marine species under pressure.The species has already been blamed for reducing soft-shell clam populations in Maine. Evidence also suggests that green crabs threaten aquatic plants, including eelgrass, which provides important habitat for marine life.Early detection and monitoring remain key to controlling the invasionThe Washington Sea Grant Crab Team identifies early detection, rapid response, monitoring and population suppression as key strategies for managing invasive green crabs.The species can have red, brown or orange colouring, according to WDFW. One identifying feature is the presence of five spines on either side of its eyes.Although the removal of more than two million crabs represents a significant control effort, researchers caution that continued monitoring and sustained intervention will be necessary to limit the species' spread and protect Washington's coastal ecosystems.You use AI every day. articles.summary: TOI correspondent from London: Just one in five (734,000) of the 3.7 million additional payroll jobs created in Britain between 2014 and 2025 went to
articles.body: TOI correspondent from London: Just one in five (734,000) of the 3.7 million additional payroll jobs created in Britain between 2014 and 2025 went to British nationals, a report by the Centre for Social Justice has revealed.This think tank, which studies the root causes of Britain’s social problems, found that EU nationals accounted for 408,000 of these jobs, while those held by non-EU nationals increased by 2.5 million.Data from HMRC shows that in Dec 2025 Indian nationals held the largest number of jobs of any foreign nationality, at 1,029,300, making up 16% of total payroll jobs held by non-UK nationals, an increase of 728,200 since 2014.“For too long, policy has prioritised adding migrants to the economy rather than unlocking the potential of even a fraction of the 6.7 million people in the hidden unemployment crisis,” the report “State of Dependency” states.“Rather than addressing the prospects, skills and productivity of the domestic population, ministers increasingly gave into public and private interest groups calling for importing labour. Worse still, after the pandemic, turbocharged immigration — the so-called ‘Boriswave’ — was explicitly used to depress wages, which policymakers feared were feeding inflation.”Most of the increase has come since Jan 2020, with non-EU payroll positions rising by 2.1 million. Yet these jobs are concentrated in lower-paid sectors such as social care, hospitality and retail, which traditionally provided routes into work for the British unemployed. The number of people receiving out-of-work benefits grew by 2.3 million over the same period.“Britain has practiced a form of ‘human quantitative easing’, importing workers to expand headline GDP while writing off millions of people who are drifting away from the labour market. But high immigration has also added substantially to the welfare bill,” it states.£14.3 billion of working-age welfare spending is now flowing to foreign nationals in Britain.The last two decades saw the British state spend £1.6 trillion on working-age benefits — over £1.1 trillion more than its capital investment on transport, science and technology, and housing combined.You use AI every day. articles.title: Houthis emerge as global threat beyond Iran control amid Saudi strikes, former envoy warns
articles.summary: Tim Lenderking warns Houthi rebels are building homegrown weapons capabilities independent of Iran, turning Yemen's conflict into a global threat.
articles.body: The Houthis are increasingly operating independently of Tehran, posing a "clear and very present danger" on the international stage as the terror group rearms and sharpens its strike capabilities, a former U.S. envoy warned Thursday. The warning came amid deadly missile and drone attacks on Saudi Arabia in recent days and growing threats to global shipping routes and critical Middle East infrastructure in the run-up. Turki al-Maliki, spokesperson for the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen, also confirmed Thursday that Houthi attacks on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh had killed 17 and injured 333 others from Oct. 7-11. Speaking at a news conference in Riyadh, al-Maliki said the Oct. 10 attack involved 10 drones, missiles and other projectiles. "King Khalid International Airport has been subjected to 20 attacks since (Oct. 1)," he noted. Tim Lenderking, who served as U.S. special envoy for Yemen from 2021 to 2025 and was posted to Saudi Arabia from 2013 to 2016, said Saudi officials had warned more than a decade ago that the Houthis would become a major threat, a prediction he says has now materialized. SAUDI FOREIGN MINISTER WARNS HOUTHI THREAT GOES GLOBAL AS TRUMP HOLDS FIRE "The Saudis were very clear to our leaders that they viewed the Houthis as a major threat," Lenderking said of his time in the kingdom a decade ago. At the time, he said, the group was "quietly building up their capability, burnishing their narrative of why they sought to lead Yemen as a messianic group, as a group from northern Yemen, with an agenda, with a mission." The Houthis had emerged as a religious and political movement in Yemen in the 1990s, but their ties to Iran developed into a military partnership after 2014, when Tehran expanded its assistance and training during Yemen's civil war. "The Houthis don't really need the Iranians anymore," Lenderking, a former acting assistant secretary for Near Eastern affairs at the U.S. State Department, continued, adding it was still "a very important relationship that "enabled the Houthis to become the powerful force that they are." Lenderking, now a distinguished diplomatic fellow at the Middle East Institute (MEI), said, over time, the Houthis had developed their own "homegrown indigenous capability" as they capitalized on any disunity across the Gulf region. Saturday's missile and drone attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh raised concerns that President Donald Trump could be drawn into a broader regional conflict as Saudi Arabia seeks U.S. assistance. Asked whether the U.S. would defend Saudi Arabia against further attacks, Trump said, "You'll find out soon." NEW RISK FOR US CONSUMERS AS IRAN-BACKED ATTACKS THREATEN A SECOND MAJOR OIL CHOKEPOINT Speaking at an MEI briefing, Lenderking said the Houthis' sophisticated weapons and targeting capabilities have transformed the group from a regional insurgency into an international security threat. "They have the capability to hit around the region, including up into the northern reaches of the Red Sea. So, this is a regional problem, and given the fact that the Houthis control the west coast of Yemen," Lenderking said. "It's an international problem now." Lenderking cited the precision of the Riyadh airport attack as evidence of the Houthis' growing capabilities compared with earlier strikes during the Gaza conflict. "They can hit things better. Now, they are hitting Terminal Four of Riyadh Airport, very specifically. It's a clear and very present danger," he said. The Houthis reportedly launched multiple drones followed by cruise and ballistic missiles that traveled more than 620 miles to Riyadh, prompting an investigation into possible Saudi air defense failures, according to The Associated Press, citing regional officials. Saudi forces intercepted two more ballistic missiles targeting Riyadh on Monday. On Tuesday, a Houthi strike caused damage to Aramco's headquarters in Dhahran, sparking a fire that spread across several floors, Reuters reported. Lenderking said the Houthis have built extensive weapons supply chains, smuggling networks and domestic financing operations that allow them to sustain attacks without relying solely on Tehran. HOUTHIS ENTER US 'KILL BOX' AFTER SEIZING RED SEA 'CORK,' FORMER PENTAGON OFFICIAL WARNS "They get a lot of supplies off the open market through the internet, through commercial exchanges. They have a very well entrenched smuggling network, from big boats onto small boats, onto tiny boats, on the pack animals, on people's backs. "They are able to move things undetected through government terrain, even through various borders and with a lot of wide open space there. They are constantly moving, building, resupplying, restocking, innovating." The group's self-sufficiency also extends to financing. Lenderking said the Houthis generate revenue through black-market oil sales, taxation and extortion while also forcing families to provide recruits, allowing the group to continue fighting even if Iranian assistance is cut off. "They have had support from Iran over the years, so they have money in the bank from that," Lenderking said. "They relied on sales of black market oil in the past. They extort Yemeni transport companies, businesses. They tax people in areas that they control. They force many families to offer up a son to fight on the front lines." The Houthis' expanding arsenal has raised concerns about potential Chinese involvement in their weapons supply networks. OIL SQUEEZE TIGHTENS AS IRAN-BACKED ATTACKS CRIPPLE HORMUZ ESCAPE ROUTES Yemen's government has accused the rebels of seeking Chinese components for medium-range ballistic missiles, raising concerns about the group's access to advanced military technology. "There is a Chinese connection here that's very detrimental," Lenderking warned, adding that front companies have helped the group obtain weapons through commercial channels. Lenderking warned that the Houthis could also target Saudi energy facilities, pipelines and desalination plants, infrastructure critical to the kingdom's economy and water supply. "The Houthis have hit pipelines," he said. "They have diesel plants and other energy infrastructure in their sights." Attacks on such facilities could disrupt global energy markets, maritime commerce and regional stability. The Houthis also control Yemen's western coastline along the Red Sea, a vital shipping corridor connecting Europe and Asia. With the rebels now capable of striking targets hundreds of miles away, Lenderking warned that the threat extends far beyond Yemen's borders. "One blast at Riyadh Airport is a huge statement," the expert said. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "That's why I come back to the fact that this is an international conflict," he said, adding that "immediate action is required."

articles.title: Italian farmer gave up a third of her rice fields for wildlife, creating Italy’s only recorded nesting site for a rare bird
articles.summary: Italian rice farmer Alice Cerutti has restored about a third of her 110-hectare farm to its natural state, creating wetlands and woodland that now support
articles.body: Italian rice farmer Alice Cerutti has restored about a third of her 110-hectare farm to its natural state, creating wetlands and woodland that now support rare wildlife. At Cascina Oschina farm on the Vercelli plain in north-west Italy, she has planted more than 10,000 native plants, helping butterflies and dragonflies thrive and attracting rare birds.According to Agence France-Presse (AFP), the restored wetlands have also become the only recorded nesting site in Italy for the black-tailed godwit. Cerutti continues to grow rice, including historic varieties that she says withstand drought and extreme heat better than modern ones.Her approach comes as Italy's rice sector faces rising production costs, imports and increasingly severe droughts. By making space for nature, she is working to protect biodiversity while continuing to produce rice in a changing climate.How an Italian rice farmer turned a third of her land into a wildlife havenAlice Cerutti took over her family’s Cascina Oschina farm in 2012. She has restored about a third of its 110 hectares, including 25 hectares converted into wetlands.The farm lies on the Vercelli plain between Milan and Turin, where golden rice fields now remain alongside woodland and wetlands. Cerutti has planted more than 10,000 native plants, including oaks, alders, ash and hornbeams.Cerutti says butterfly and dragonfly numbers have risen sharply since planting began. Her farm is an EU-certified protected area. The restored habitats now support rare species, including the Large Copper butterfly, while providing a refuge for birds in Italy's rice-growing region.Why a rare bird is nesting in the restored wetlandsThe wetlands have become an important habitat for wildlife, including the black-tailed godwit. Cerutti's property is now the only recorded Italian nesting site for this bird. She said the number of migrating birds in the rice-growing region had fallen by 80% over the past 15 years.The farm's restored landscape also supports rare insects, including the Large Copper butterfly, alongside butterflies and dragonflies that, she says, have increased since native plants were introduced. Cerutti's work has changed part of a landscape that monks transformed from marshland into rice fields around 400 years ago.Instead of using all the available land for crops, she has returned a substantial area to wetlands and woodland, prioritising biodiversity alongside agricultural production.How historic rice varieties help the farm withstand heat and droughtCerutti grows red and black rice alongside historic varieties such as Carnaroli Classico and Arborio Classico. These varieties produce smaller but higher-quality yields than modern ones and withstand drought and extreme heat better.Carnaroli Classico has awns, which are slender, bristle-like extensions thought to help protect the rice against heat and cold. Cerutti said she grew her Carnaroli Classico without using a single gram of chemical fertiliser. Instead, she uses green manure and legume crops to enrich the soil. Around 1,200 sheep graze on crops between rice harvests, leaving organic matter behind.Why restoring nature matters as Italy's rice sector faces growing pressureItaly is Europe's largest rice producer, but the sector faces rising production costs, a flood of Asian imports, and droughts made more frequent and intense by human-driven climate change. Agricultural organisation Coldiretti estimated that around 25% of the country’s rice production may be lost to heat this year.As some farmers turn to dry-seeding, which avoids the need for continuous flooding, agronomist Giovanni Molina told AFP that flooded rice fields play an important role in recharging underground aquifers. Meanwhile, Cerutti has given up some productive land to restore natural habitats.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: TSA warns travelers about seasonal mistake that could trigger airport security delays
articles.summary: Halloween travelers wearing costume makeup, bringing metal-heavy accessories and carrying props could face delays and challenges at airports, the TSA is warning.
articles.body: Travelers planning to fly in costume this Halloween could face unexpected hurdles at airport security. While costumes themselves are generally allowed, certain accessories, masks, special makeup and metal pieces can create problems at TSA checkpoints, according to the agency's website. Travelers wearing elaborate face coverings or heavy costume makeup may be asked to remove it if their identity cannot be verified during screening. POPULAR PANTRY STAPLE COULD GET YOU STOPPED AT AIRPORT SECURITY UNDER LITTLE-KNOWN TSA RULE Keith Jeffries, vice president of K2 Security Screening Group and a former federal security director for TSA at Los Angeles International Airport, told Fox News Digital that facial recognition technology is becoming more common at airports. "If you're wearing … Halloween costume-style makeup, and it can't recognize you, that's going to create some challenges," he said. Costume props packed in luggage can also raise security concerns, particularly when they resemble weapons or other prohibited items. Replica explosives, including fake bombs and grenades, are not allowed in carry-on or checked luggage, according to TSA guidance. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER Weapon-like props, such as fake knives, swords, guns and pitchforks, should also stay out of carry-on bags, experts say. Some may be permitted in checked luggage, depending on the item. Jeffries recalled seeing similar issues during his 20 years with the TSA, including travelers trying to bring replicas of "Lucille," the barbed-wire-covered baseball bat featured on "The Walking Dead," through security. "Of course, that just can't go through the checkpoint," he said, noting that it could be placed in checked luggage. Metal-heavy costumes could create another headache by triggering screening equipment and potentially leading to additional screening, Jeffries said. CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES "That's going to cause all kinds of challenges and just slow the whole process down," he said. Travelers packing makeup must also follow standard TSA liquid restrictions. Liquid makeup in carry-ons generally must be in containers of 3.4 ounces or less, while larger quantities should go into checked luggage, according to the TSA. For travelers bringing more elaborate costumes or accessories, Jeffries recommended packing these items rather than wearing them through security. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ "My biggest recommendation [is] put all of that stuff in your checked luggage, even if you normally don't like to check a bag," he said. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "Pack your costumes, go to where you're going and enjoy your fun," Jeffries said. Fox News Digital reached out to the TSA for further details and comment.

articles.title: Autistic teen lured to fake Snapchat meetup, brutally beaten by group of teens: report
articles.summary: Video captured the violent beating of a 15-year-old boy with autism near a Stawell train station after he was lured through a Snapchat meetup.
articles.body: Three teenage boys were charged after a 15-year-old boy with autism was beaten and robbed near a train station in Australia in a violent attack captured on video as other teenagers watched. The assault happened Oct. 5 in Stawell, a town in the Australian state of Victoria, after the victim was reportedly lured to the area through a Snapchat meetup arranged with two girls, according to Australian news outlet news.com.au. Video of the attack shows several teenagers punching and kicking the boy, knocking him to the ground and repeatedly striking him as he attempts to get away. One attacker demands the victim hand over his shoes before the group allows him to leave. TEXAS TEENS ACCUSED OF USING DATING APPS TO LURE YOUNG MEN INTO VIOLENT ROBBERIES THAT LEFT ONE VICTIM SHOT Victoria Police announced Tuesday that detectives had charged one 14-year-old boy and two 15-year-old boys after an investigation. Detectives from the Northern Grampians Crime Investigation Unit executed four search warrants in the region before arresting the teenagers, police said. All three face charges of affray, robbery, recklessly causing injury and theft. They are expected to appear in a children's court at a later date. TEEN BURGLARY RING LINKED TO NEARLY 80 BAY AREA BREAK-INS DISMANTLED AFTER MONTHS-LONG INVESTIGATION: PD Police said a fourth boy who was not present when the search warrants were served would be interviewed as part of the ongoing investigation. The victim, who also has epilepsy, suffered soft tissue injuries and possible head injuries, according to news.com.au. His mother told the outlet doctors were conducting additional scans to determine whether he had bleeding in his brain. "I’m just lucky to have him alive. … He’s having nightmares," she said. TEEN PUNCHED AND KICKED INTO A COMA AFTER KNICKS-SPURS ALTERCATION NEAR MADISON SQUARE GARDEN: POLICE The boy has since returned home but is afraid to go outside, his mother told the outlet. Superintendent Dan Davison acknowledged the concern the attack had caused in the Stawell community and said police had been working to identify those responsible. "Since last Monday, local uniform police and detectives have been working tirelessly to identify those involved and hold them to account, and this important work will continue," Davison said in a news release. "There is never any excuse for violence in our community, and we will not accept it in any form. "Detectives are continuing to investigate the matter, and while we are treating it as an isolated incident, additional patrols will take place across Stawell to ensure our community not only is safe but feels safe." articles.title: White House prepares plans to use 'mother of all bombs' on Iran: Report
articles.summary: The White House and Pentagon have prepared plans to deploy the US military’s largest non-nuclear bomb against Iran, including potential strikes on energy
articles.body: The White House and Pentagon have prepared plans to deploy the US military’s largest non-nuclear bomb against Iran, including potential strikes on energy infrastructure and nuclear sites, if President Donald Trump orders a resumption of combat operations, according to reports by CBS News and CNN.The plans include the GBU-43/B Massive Ordnance Air Blast (MOAB), commonly known as the “mother of all bombs”, which weighs more than 21,000 pounds and is designed to unleash a massive blast across a wide area. CNN, citing US officials familiar with military planning, reported that potential targets included energy infrastructure and the suspected nuclear facility at Pickaxe Mountain.CBS News also reported that the White House and Pentagon had drawn up plans to use the weapon against Iranian military sites. The reports come as the Trump administration considers its options for ending a conflict that has continued for more than six months, with no clear indication of an imminent diplomatic breakthrough.A Pentagon official told CBS News: "The Department of War plans for a wide range of operational scenarios to execute Presidential and Secretary level direction and to ensure mission success in any operational environment."A White House spokesperson said: "We do not comment on sensitive military plans that may or may not exist. President Trump keeps all options on the table to ensure that Iran can never have a nuclear weapon."Last week, Trump said the US would not attack Iran before the midterm elections. He also spoke of "productive conversations" with Tehran without providing details.However, the inclusion of the MOAB in military planning does not mean Trump has authorised its use. CNN reported that US military planners were also preparing for possible Iranian retaliation if further strikes were ordered.The weapon was used in combat for the first time in April 2017, during Trump's first presidency, when the US military dropped it on an Islamic State tunnel complex in Afghanistan.Despite its enormous destructive power, the MOAB is not designed to penetrate deeply buried targets. CNN reported that officials had questioned whether it could destroy facilities such as Pickaxe Mountain, believed to be protected by layers of granite.The bomb detonates before hitting the ground, spreading its blast across a large area rather than burrowing underground like a specialised bunker-buster. Its potential use against energy infrastructure could also raise concerns about civilian casualties, particularly near populated areas.Military planners have considered the weapon as one option for increasing pressure on Tehran, although officials have questioned whether additional strikes alone would achieve Washington's broader objectives or force Iran to capitulate.You use AI every day. articles.title: Jeffrey Donaldson: Former DUP leader poses huge 'risk-management' headache for prison staff
articles.summary: Jeffrey Donaldson was sentenced to 15 years for committing sex abuse, including one of rape, against two women when they were children.
articles.body:
Protecting convicted paedophile Jeffrey Donaldson from harm inside jail will be a "massive risk-management headache" for prison bosses, according to a former governor.

The ex-Democratic Unionist Party (DUP) leader was given a 15-year sentence on Thursday after being convicted of 18 counts of sex abuse, including rape, against two women when they were children.

Ian Acheson, who spent about a decade working for HM Prison Service, said Donaldson, the former Lagan Valley MP, faced risks from fellow inmates.

Acheson said Donaldson represented a "very complex challenge to the Northern Ireland Prison Service".

"There are always hierarchies within prisons - and there are even hierarchies within sex offenders - and the lowest of the low and the most vulnerable in terms of hostility from others are those who've been convicted of sexual violence against a minor."

But he said it would also be necessary to "examine potential political or sectarian targeting" relating to Donaldson's leadership of the DUP and his service in the Ulster Defence Regiment, a former Army unit.

"The prison has a duty of care to protect him and he is uniquely vulnerable," Acheson told BBC Radio Ulster's Talkback programme.

"Maghaberry, in previous inspections, has indicated that it operates an integrated regime, where sex offenders can be safely managed in the wider prison community.

"I don't think that is remotely viable for Jeffrey Donaldson, given those offence characteristics and his background.

"So either he is kept, in effect, in conditions of solitary confinement for years and years or another solution has to be found.

"I don't think it's acceptable to keep him in conditions of solitary confinement - it may not even be legal."

Donaldson spends up to18 hours a day in his cell at Maghaberry, which holds about 1,600 inmates.

It is thought he has been put in the Moyola Unit, which primarily houses prisoners with health issues, for his own safety, as it isolates him from risk of attack or verbal abuse from other prisoners.

He is believed to spend much of his day reading books from the prison library.

Acheson said there was a "precedent within the UK" to transfer prisoners within different jurisdictions, therefore Donaldson "could be potentially compulsorily transferred" to another jail.

Donaldson was convicted in June of sex offences against two females referred to in his trial as Victim A and Victim B.

He was sentenced to 11 years for his crimes against Victim B and four years for offences against Victim A.

During sentencing, Judge Paul Ramsey said Donaldson's crimes had led to a "catastrophic descent into disgrace".

Donaldson, who denied the charges, is seeking to appeal his convictions .

He will also be required to sign the Sex Offenders Register for life.

Jeffrey Donaldson's time in politics began in 1985 when he was elected for the Ulster Unionist Party (UUP) as an MLA in South Down.

In 1997, Donaldson became the MP for Lagan Valley, representing the UUP. He would remain an MP until 2024.

However, in 2003, he quit the UUP and defected to the DUP.

Donaldson was awarded a knighthood in the 2016 Queen's Birthday Honours list, and, in 2021, became leader of the DUP .

He remained leader until March 2024, when he was charged with sexual offences of a historical nature .

He was found guilty of all 18 child sex abuse charges, including one count of rape, in June 2026.

Donaldson subsequently asked for his knighthood to be forfeited and tendered his resignation from the Privy Council with immediate effect.

articles.title: Are student protests being manipulated ahead France’s presidential election?
articles.summary: France's prime minister has suggested that student anger is being weaponised, as the unions and other protesters prepare to take to the streets too.
articles.body:
The French passion for protest is legendary in Europe.

Over the last few years, we have regularly witnessed farmers angry about costly regulations lobbing manure at local mayoral offices, while masked youths periodically hurl homemade grenades at riot police in disadvantaged city suburbs.

For over three weeks now, thousands of students have barricaded entry to high schools and taken their grievances to the streets.

This Saturday, hundreds of new demonstrations have been announced across France.

Students are expected to be joined by workers' unions and key figures from the so-called "yellow vest" movement.

France's prime minister, Sébastien Lecornu, suggested this week that student anger was being manipulated as politics heats up ahead of next year's presidential election.

The gilets jaunes (yellow vests) demonstrated against cost-of-living hikes for over a year from 2018 - becoming one of the longest-lived protest movements in French history.

Jérôme Rodrigues, a prominent gilets jaunes activist, has used Instagram to encourage people to join Saturday's demonstrations.

The protests should give a voice to those who "want to be able to live decently, no longer have to count every cent, and no longer have to choose between eating and driving", he said in a video.

"Anger has no political party. An empty fridge has no political party," he added.

So what is going on in the EU's second largest economy?

Social unrest, government borrowing costs at eye-watering highs, a deeply divided French parliament and an apparent revolving door of exasperated French prime ministers - six prime ministers over the last five years - all claiming to want to reduce their country's public debt.

Is France at breaking-point - and what does this all mean for the eurozone currency the French are such a huge part of?

"You can't compare France to the Greece debt crisis of 2012 or Argentina in 2001. And the financial markets know it," economist Anne-Laure Delatte told me.

She is a CNRS Tenured Researcher at the Economics Department of Paris Dauphine University; a well-known face in debates on French media on the parlous state of the country's public debt.

"The markets recognised already in 2024 that we would have a budgetary problem after [snap] elections left parliament deeply divided between three [opposing political] blocs but they also realise France is a big country with the ability to raise taxes if necessary."

"Our situation is more like the UK in 2023 with Liz Truss," suggests Delatte, referring to the then UK prime minister's so-called mini budget, which triggered a sharp drop in the pound, a spike in government bond yields and soaring mortgage rates.

"The crisis was relatively short-lived because the markets recognised the UK had the financial tools to right itself."

"Here in France it would be painful, but a 4% increase in VAT would raise the 120bn euros needed to plug government debt. Investors know that," she concludes.

Maybe, in theory. And, as Delatte also points out, the European Central Bank would likely intervene if France's finances nosedived to the point where other European economies would be affected.

But with so many French citizens already visibly unhappy with the status quo, imagine the reaction if taxes were to increase, or welfare and education budgets decrease, further.

France's national motto is liberté, égalité, fraternité (freedom, equality and fraternity), but that is certainly not the sense you get on seething streets and in viral social media posts.

I met 17-year-olds Maxime, Madeleine and Elodie this week, perched on big green dustbins that have been used to block the entrance to their high school as part of the weeks' long protest.

They told me things were bad enough here, in the 3rd district of Paris, with holes in classroom walls, swelling class sizes and a dearth of teaching staff, but the teenagers were more than aware, they said, that the situation was far worse in their capital city's disadvantaged suburbs.

"France likes to speak of égalité ," they told me "but the reality is the poor here are prejudiced against, while the rich benefit."

None of them will be old enough to vote in the presidential election in France next spring but they questioned whether the changing face of politicians in power made all that much difference anyway.

The three young women told me large-scale protests seemed the only way to get heard by French authorities.

'Everyone hates the police' – what France's school protests reveal about a divided nation

France's school protests: What lies behind the anger

France halts use of stun grenades after boy's hand blown off in student protests

They are part of a defiant French tradition.

Cultural icon Victor Hugo, the 19th-Century author of French Revolution classic Les Misérables , also an activist for the French Republic, proclaimed: " Si vous n'êtes pas contents, manifestez, criez, hurlez, mais ne subissez pas ."

("If you are not happy, protest, shout, scream but do not give up and give in.")

Amongst crowds of protesting students walking through Paris on Thursday, I came across a number of mums, with placards around their necks, reading: "Mums in solidarity."

Were they there to protest or to protect their kids, I asked? "Both!" was the emphatic response.

Gwen, 37, said she and other mothers were taking it in turns every morning to co-ordinate between students and police at their local school lock-in.

This came after mounting accusations of police brutality, denied by France's interior ministry, during protests earlier this month in which hundreds were injured and a 15-year-old boy in the town of Lens lost a hand.

France's interior minister has since suspended the use of stun grenades by police at high school demonstrations.

Gwen told me she did not mind that her son was missing weeks of school as a result of the lock-ins. "It's a far better education for him to wake up to his civic duty and to fight for what is just in society," she said.

At Thursday's demo I also came across 17-year-old Lola and her mother, Sandrine, sharing a placard that said revolution was the most beautiful expression of humanity.

"My mum took to the streets in '68," Lola said proudly. "Now it's my turn. No point in waiting for the presidential election in France. We want change now."

Student protests in Paris in May 1968 are the stuff of legend in France. Demands for better education inspired workers to join the marches which turned into the ­biggest general strike in French ­history. It set the standard for revolutionary upheaval for a generation and is credited with creating new opportunities for the French left.

Now, though, with six months to go before an already fraught presidential election in France, there are accusations that the hard left, under presidential hopeful Jean-Luc Mélenchon, is weaponising student frustration.

"Members of [Mélenchon's] France Insoumise (LFI) are instrumentalising the high school movement for their electoral advantage," said Sébastien Lecornu on Wednesday. He accused them of encouraging protests, then going through the motions of condemning any violence.

"This hypocrisy damages France," said Lecornu.

But "Mélenchon for President!" is a chant you often hear amongst the students in the streets.

Supporters applaud his desire for a wealth tax in France, for lowering the voting age to 16 and for being the only presidential candidate to turn up to French schools to examine the state of them, several demonstrators told me.

For Marine Le Pen, the nationalist anti-immigration favourite in France's presidential race, the solution is cutting the country's €11bn contribution to the EU's budget.

There is, though, reason to doubt that any new French president, from the left or the right, will be able to break the impasse over France's finances.

France is far from alone in Europe right now faced with an ageing population, a generous welfare state to run and a national economy squeezed by outside pressures such as US President Donald Trump's trade tariffs and the war in the Persian Gulf.

Whether in France, Germany, Sweden or Italy, there is an inherent tension between politicians who hesitate to tell voters the truth about shrinking public finances, the defence establishment's demand for higher defence spending and citizens' insistence on improved public services.

In France, that pressure is particularly acute. French public expenditure, at about 57% GDP, is one of the steepest amongst wealthy nations worldwide.

Social spending, particularly on pensions, is exceptionally large, while French citizens pay one of the highest overall tax and social contribution burdens in Europe. Simply put, they expect a welfare and public service bang for their buck.

But economist Anne-Laure Delatte does not believe having a new president will ease her country's financial migraine.

"We need constitutional change. A new system. A new Republic," she told me.

"Our Fifth Republic is centred around a powerful president. Parliament is there to block him or her rather than to find consensus or to make new laws."

For France to progress, she says, that has to change.

The French parliamentary election that follows the 2027 presidential vote is likely to be as divided as ever, she believes: "We need a system where MPs have more power and should learn consensus and coalition-building from our European neighbours."

In her opinion, education had to be protected and funds better distributed. It was an investment in France's financial future, she told me.

"Our current system of inequality in schooling and low wages for teachers means we lose out from benefiting from the best and brightest across French society. That is not only unfair on individuals but our economy ultimately loses out on innovation and productivity."

Re-writing France's constitution is not on the cards, at the moment. So, what about the here and now, I asked centrist politician Anne-Catherine Loisier.

She's a senator for the Centrist Union in France's upper house of parliament and vice president of the parliamentary group for sciences and technology.

Loisier, along with pretty much every leading French politician across the political spectrum, says the protesting students "must feel heard".

"Our budgets are limited," she admitted, "but you don't necessarily need more money. You can make improvements by redistributing funding better. Education is a regional competence in France. Every region should take a look at local needs and address priorities accordingly. That action can be taken immediately."

I asked Loisier if she agreed with UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham, the former mayor of Greater Manchester, that regions should be given greater powers. "Absolutely," she replied. "France has traditionally been very Paris-centric but so much could be improved by decentralising the country."

"My France isn't broken. I don't recognise that image you see portrayed in the media. My country is made up of lots of Frances. Paris, the regions; northern and southern France. We need to give power back to the people. Local governments can look people in the eye directly, so voters feel they have power over their own future, rather than politicians handing them their fate from up high in Paris."

"That way I hope we can restore voters' - and students' - faith in politics."

It's a promise you hear from politicians - right and left - ahead of France's huge elections next year.

But opinion polls here, as across most of Europe, indicate public faith in the political class is in dwindling supply.

articles.body: SRINAGAR: A crucial meeting on autonomy between a ministry of home affairs (MHA) subcommittee and Ladakhi representatives in Leh on Wednesday ended inconclusively, with both sides agreeing to hold talks again on Oct 22 in New Delhi.“The MHA team gave a presentation of its draft proposal and we submitted our draft. articles.title: It’s a woman’s choice
articles.summary: Courts must respect a woman’s right to decide whether she wants to continue a pregnancy Three recent cases in High Courts show that women still do not
articles.body: Courts must respect a woman’s right to decide whether she wants to continue a pregnancyThree recent cases in High Courts show that women still do not always get to decide for themselves whether to have an abortion after 20 weeks of pregnancy.In 2022, the Supreme Court said that every woman, whether married or unmarried, has the right to decide whether she wants to have a child. This right is protected by the Constitution, which promises people dignity, privacy and personal freedom.Yet, four years later, the Bombay High Court had to ask for a change in an official form so that unmarried women could also apply for abortions. The court allowed one woman to have an abortion, but said its decision should not be treated as a rule for future cases. Why should a woman’s right to make decisions about her own body be treated as a special exception?In another case, the Bombay High Court refused an abortion to a woman whose husband had hidden the fact that he was already married. She left him and later discovered she was pregnant. The court rejected her request because she did not fit into certain legal categories, such as being divorced or separated. This raises an important question: should a woman be denied a choice because her personal situation does not fit neatly into the rules?In a third case, the Madhya Pradesh High Court allowed a married woman who was heading for a divorce to end a 13-week pregnancy. The court recognised that the decision belonged to her.These cases show that different courts sometimes interpret abortion laws differently. Doctors’ opinions, medical tests and judges’ personal views can all affect the outcome.But every woman’s situation is different. The Supreme Court has already made the basic principle clear: forcing a woman to continue an unwanted pregnancy goes against her right to make decisions about her own life and body.Courts must remember this and respect women’s freedom to make their own reproductive choices.Disclaimer: Views expressed above are the author's own.

articles.title: Diwali cleaning DIY: How to make your own reusable floor-cleaning cloth from old clothes
articles.summary: Diwali cleaning has a way of piling up old clothes in the cupboard, worn-out t-shirts, faded nightwear and soft cotton kurtas that no longer get worn but
articles.body: Diwali cleaning has a way of piling up old clothes in the cupboard, worn-out t-shirts, faded nightwear and soft cotton kurtas that no longer get worn but still feel too good to bin. Instead of buying disposable mop heads and wipes, you can turn them into sturdy floor-cleaning cloths that cost nothing and wash again and again. A homemade cloth is also a good way to cut down on waste at a time of year when the house tends to fill up with packaging. Here’s how to make one in five easy steps, with no sewing machine needed.Choose the right old clothesThe best fabrics are soft, absorbent cotton, such as old t-shirts, cotton sarees, bedsheets, towels or kurtas. Cotton soaks up water well and leaves very little lint behind. Avoid anything with sequins, heavy embroidery, thick seams, zips or buttons, since these can scratch your floor, and be careful with synthetics, which tend to push the water around instead of absorbing it. Wash the clothes first and let them dry, so they’re clean and any dye has already run.Cut the fabric into usable piecesLay the fabric out flat and cut it into squares or rectangles. A piece about 12 by 12 inches is handy for wiping by hand, while a larger piece of around 20 by 30 inches works better wrapped around a mop or flat floor-wiper. T-shirts can also be cut into long strips, which you can knot or braid together into a mop head. Straight, even edges make the cloth easier to fold, though they don’t need to be perfect. Use sharp scissors and discard any thin or torn areas.Layer for extra absorbencyA single thin layer of cloth soaks up very little, so a thicker pad does a better job. Stack two to three layers of fabric on top of each other, ideally with the softest cotton on the outside and a towel or thicker piece in the middle. Fold the stack neatly in half to make a pad. This helps the cloth hold more water and clean more floor before it needs rinsing. For a sturdier cloth, a thicker core of an old towel works well, and anything too stiff can go on the underside only if your floor allows.Secure the edgesTo stop the layers from slipping apart, secure them together. If you sew, a simple running stitch or a zigzag stitch around the edges works. If you don’t, use a few safety pins, or a strong fabric glue where the cloth won’t be soaked for long. For a no-stitch mop head, wrap the cloth around a flat mop or a broom and tie it firmly in place with a strip of the same fabric. Check it holds before you start mopping. The aim is a pad that stays in place without bunching up.Use it, wash it and keep it freshDampen the cloth with plain water or your usual floor-cleaning mix, wring it well, and wipe the floor in sections, rinsing it often so you aren’t spreading dirt around. After use, rinse it out right away, then wash it in hot water with detergent, separately from clothes you wear, and dry it fully in the sun to keep it from smelling musty. Replace the cloth when it wears thin. Keep a few on rotation, and don’t use the same one on the bathroom and kitchen floors.Disclaimer: This article is intended for general informational and household purposes only. Always test a new cleaning cloth or cleaning solution on a small, hidden patch of your floor first, as results can vary with the floor type and finish. Avoid soaking wooden or laminate floors, and wash reusable cloths separately from clothing. Keep cleaning supplies away from children and pets.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: At least 5 people believed to be dead after shooting at Oregon elementary school: Reports
articles.summary: A gunman opened fire at Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, Ore., before being shot dead. There are multiple victims.
articles.body:
At least five people are believed to be dead after a gunman opened fire at Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, Ore., on Thursday, according to multiple outlets . The shooter was also killed, authorities said.

Police first received reports of an active shooter at 12:59 p.m. local time, when an unknown man had fired a gun into a car before entering the school, where he continued shooting, according to the Bend Police Department .

Officers arrived on the scene within three minutes of the initial report. Moments later, the shooter was reported dead, potentially shot by a bystander, police said.

Authorities confirmed there had been multiple victims, including children, but did not disclose details. Two people were transported to a nearby hospital. Their status is unknown. It's unclear if the suspect was included among the five.

"We are stunned and heartbroken by this senseless tragedy," Bend-La Pine Schools Superintendent Steven Cook wrote in a statement. "We extend our deepest sympathy to the families and to everyone affected by this violence. No words can adequately express the grief our community is experiencing. Our immediate priorities are caring for our students and staff and assisting law enforcement and emergency responders."

FBI Director Kash Patel said the agency was on the scene assisting in the investigation.

Bend-La Pine Schools said it had set up a family reunification site at a nearby church and that all of its schools would be closed on Friday, and any activities and athletic events would be canceled.

"As we learn more about the tragic event at Silver Rail Elementary in Bend today, we must come together and support each other, neighbor to neighbor, Oregonian to Oregonian," Gov. Tina Kotek said in a statement . "No community should have to live through this day." This is a developing story. Check back for updates.

articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Thursday said it will be problematic if every citizen becomes a journalist as PILs sought protection of the right to freedom of
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Thursday said it will be problematic if every citizen becomes a journalist as PILs sought protection of the right to freedom of expression of freelancers, independent journalists and reel-makers who descend in large numbers at protest venues already teeming with hordes of accredited reporters from registered media houses.Senior advocate Indira Jaising complained to a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi that Delhi Police did not recognise independent and freelance journalists covering the protests and insisted on Press Information Bureau (PIB) accreditation. She said there must be a national protocol for police not to obstruct the professional work of any journalist who has an identity card from the employer.CJI Kant, however, struck a note of caution. “We must also keep one thing in mind. If everyone starts becoming a journalist, it will create problems for every other person,” he said. Justice Bagchi said, “It will require a detailed examination whether the right to freedom of expression will empower every citizen of this country to be a journalist. That is difficult. There are layers of protection for accredited journalists, those employed in registered media houses or whether they are freelance journalists, influencers or reel-makers.”CJI Kant said, “The issue requires detailed examination — whether there should be a certain category of journalists to whom extra level of protection should be given.” Justice Bagchi added, “The Working Journalists Act makes classes among journalists. We must examine all that.”Solicitor general Tushar Mehta said in the present era of digital technology, any person with a mobile phone could claim to be an independent or freelance journalist when he/she would, in fact, be only making reels to garner popularity on social media to earn money by either presenting one-sided stories or sensationalising incidents.Mehta supported the contention that women journalists should not be harrassed, but argued that the same consideration should be extended to women police personnel as well.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Daily Career Horoscope, October 16, 2026: Success, challenges, and breakthroughs; Know about your career
articles.summary: Aries Healthy competition at work can encourage you to achieve at a better level, as long as you keep your focus on improving your own productivity
articles.body: AriesHealthy competition at work can encourage you to achieve at a better level, as long as you keep your focus on improving your own productivity instead of beating someone else. See what the strong performers around you are doing right and use that as inspiration to enhance your methods. Don’t be sucked by comparisons, workplace politics or unneeded proving. Competition is good when it makes you more disciplined and better at what you do. Be better. Be consistent. Be measurable. Instead of responding to every challenge around you, let superior performance establish your position.TaurusYour ability to manage people with tact can make professional interactions quite easy. Not everyone will respond to the same communication style so make sure you tailor to the personality of the person. When dealing with arguments, expectations, or sensitive workplace issues, take the time to listen before you answer. Diplomacy is not about avoiding hard conversations. Diplomacy is about having hard conversations without building the opposition that wasn’t necessary. People management abilities are an important way to resolve conflicts quickly, promote cooperation and develop trust This skill might be especially helpful if you’re managing teams, clients or joint tasks.GeminiBusiness owners could witness upward trends in profits and that could mean that the recent efforts are starting to create better commercial results. Don’t jump to grow because data look good, figure out what’s really driving the improvement. An initiative may also start to produce regular returns but give it loads of time to see if the pattern is something that can continue. Watch consumer response, profitability and repeat demand closely. Celebrating positive business momentum is less valuable than understanding it. We can strengthen the initiatives that are already yielding results to build a more solid base for future growth.CancerMore efforts could go into becoming noticed by someone who has some influence. Visibility can absolutely improve your career, but don’t make your contribution look forced or too theatrical. But concentrate on doing work that naturally shows your talent, dependability and good judgment. Influential people are less impressed by evident attempts to get noticed than consistent results. If you have an opportunity to showcase your work or step into more responsibility, take it and make it your own. The quality of your contribution should make the impression, not the emphasis you put on being recognized.LeoYou may receive visible recognition for your professional efforts, confirming that recent work has made a positive impression. Recognition might be in the form of feedback, more trust, or more involvement in crucial responsibilities. Take this opportunity to see what aspects of your performance are catching on and continue to refine them. Work related travel can be a valuable professional exposure and provide a refreshing change of atmosphere. Be aware of talks and contacts along the journey, as informal exchanges can occasionally be professionally useful. Recognition coupled with consistency in delivery can provide further career momentum.VirgoIf you are efficient and proactive, you will receive praise for your work. If you take the initiative without having to be reminded several times, this shows ownership and can build confidence in you as a professional that people can rely on. Expect to continue to accomplish what needs to be done, without assuming responsibility for it just because you can handle it. If you are proactive you will do so with the things that matter. Not that you are proactive with every little thing. If your contribution is valued, use it as a confirmation that you are working in the right way. Steady initiative might put you in line for more responsibility and recognition over time.LibraProfessionals may have a productive period, with potential to recruit new clients or to expand existing business relationships. Don’t use a generic sales strategy, try to discover what the prospective clients really need. Interest becomes long-term professional partnerships with good communication, follow-up on schedule, and reliable delivery. Not every lead deserves equal pursuit if some have limited strategic importance. A chosen method can improve task management and conversion. For example, new client acquisition is very lucrative where it provides repeat business, not only short-term professional engagement.ScorpioBusiness owners might want to consider promotional techniques to increase visibility. Before you start spending money on marketing, get clear on what you want potential buyers to remember about your firm. Promotion is more effective when you are precise, not just frequent. Find out which channels you already get meaningful inquiries from and focus your resources there, rather than trying everything everywhere. Try out new methods on a small scale and gauge the response. More visibility is good for growing a business, but the best results come from visibility tied to clear positioning and a relevant audience.SagittariusIt could be a new or unfamiliar work obligation that could challenge your flexibility. Think of it as an opportunity to extend your capabilities rather than becoming awkward because the assignment is different from your normal work. Understand what is expected of you, understand what you know, get help where there are real gaps in knowledge. But you don’t have to learn everything at once. Willingness to learn and the ability to be dependable can make a great impression in a professional setting. Taking on new tasks that you have not had before can be very helpful in broadening your expertise and preparing you for other positions that may be more sophisticated or different in the future.CapricornNew ways of thinking can sharpen your professional practices and improve the way you approach tasks that you already know. Just because something worked in the past doesn’t mean there’s no room for more efficiency. Be open to experimenting with new tools, workflows, or communication techniques. Innovation does not always mean radical change. A little change if regularly made can save time or boost output. Try innovative techniques on a practical level before you replace old systems wholesale. Improving the way work gets done can increase productivity and professional reputation.AquariusYou seem to be making some headway on the professional front and this seems promising. This might be a good time to capitalize on the momentum you already have. Don’t try to go for a bigger breakthrough right once, find what’s working already and build those habits or routines. Short term improvement can be made more reliable by consistent implementation. Keep an eye on your outstanding tasks so that unfinished business doesn’t stall positive momentum. This is a good time to show you are reliable and build on what you have already achieved. Disciplined follow-up to progressive preparation for larger professional possibilities can achieve steady improvement.PiscesYour work environment may change to give you opportunities that you didn’t have before. A change in duties, team structure, processes, leadership or working arrangements may initially need to be adjusted to but may also expose you to good experiences. Don’t dismiss the change too soon just because it interrupts your regular routines. Look at the fresh opportunities it presents and where your abilities may be used to add value. Changes in career can be like that too. At first you don’t know what you’re doing, but then you figure out what you can do. Flexibility can allow you to turn a change at work into something that contributes to your career growth and development in a meaningful way.This article is written by, Sidhharrth S Kumaar, Registered Pharmacist, Astro Numerologist, Life & Relationship Coach, Vaastu Expert, IKS Expert, I Ching Expert, Energy Healer, Music Therapist, Author of “Think like a Sage Lead like a CEO” series and Chief Astro Strategy Officer (CASO), NumroVani.Get the latest astrology news and horoscope updates. articles.title: Kash Patel demands MS NOW apologize after network's false report claiming FBI director visited Russia
articles.summary: FBI Director Kash Patel is demanding an apology from MS NOW after the network falsely claimed he "landed in Russia" for meetings, which was debunked.
articles.body: FBI Director Kash Patel is calling on MS NOW to issue more than a correction after the network falsely reported he had landed in Russia. "MS NOW put me in Russia based on two anonymous sources. I was in Virginia, honoring law enforcement at Liberty University. The network had to correct its false report," Patel wrote on X Thursday. "This was a basic verification failure," he continued. "They were wrong about my location, and they are wrong about the successes of this FBI and our partnership with State, Local, and Tribal Law Enforcement. If a network cannot confirm where I was before putting it on air, how can the public trust its reporting on the work our agents and officers do every day? "This is bigger than a false story about me. The men and women of law enforcement deserve accurate reporting while they protect communities and take violent criminals off our streets. Three apologies are owed: to this FBI, to the law enforcement community, and to the American People." MS NOW ISSUES CORRECTION AFTER REPORTING KASH PATEL 'LANDED IN RUSSIA' WHILE HE WAS ACTUALLY IN VIRGINIA MS NOW did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment. A spokesperson previously pointed to the network's on-air correction. On Wednesday, MS NOW anchor Peter Alexander informed viewers of "breaking news" that Patel had "landed in Russia" to attend meetings. MS NOW justice correspondent Ken Dilanian's report cited two FBI sources and said that there were concerns within the agency about Patel's alleged visit to the Kremlin. MS NOW REPORTER PANS KASH PATEL'S 'BASICALLY BOGUS' FBI STATS AFTER TOUTING BIDEN-ERA CRIME DATA Shortly after MS NOW ran its breaking news report, the FBI Rapid Response X account mocked the liberal network, noting that Patel was actually in Virginia for a law enforcement appreciation event. Dilanian later issued a correction. "I want to correct reporting from earlier today," he told MS NOW viewers. "I reported that two sources had told us that FBI Director Kash Patel had landed in Russia for a planned trip that had been reported about recently. We've since learned that Patel did not, in fact, land in Russia today and remains in the U.S. The FBI did not answer our questions when we asked them about it." "But we do know now that he has not already landed in Russia, as we reported earlier," Dilanian continued. "The timing of any potential trip remains unclear. Again, we regret this error, and we are transparent about when we make errors." FBI DIRECTOR KASH PATEL, NEW YORK TIMES CLASH OVER PAPER'S CLAIM ITS REPORTER WAS 'INVESTIGATED' There was been speculation among critics that Dilanian's false report was the result of an effort to expose leakers within the FBI. An FBI official would neither confirm nor deny whether leadership had conducted such an operation but said the two leakers involved would "likely" be identified as a result. articles.body: Candace Owens has reignited questions about Andrew Kolvet's arrival in Provo following Charlie Kirk's killing, claiming Erika Kirk failed to answer a direct question about whether Kolvet travelled with his wife. In a social media post, Grace Ashford highlighted Owens' account of the exchange, questioning why Erika appeared unable to confirm the travel arrangements. Owens says Kolvet previously described flying alone before collapsing into Erika's arms on the tarmac. She now suspects the accounts do not match, although her claims have not independently established that anyone deliberately misled her.Candace Owens questions Erika Kirk over Andrew Kolvet's alleged tarmac hugOwens said her first conversation with Kolvet left her with a clear impression that he had travelled alone to Provo after Charlie's death. Recalling his description, she said:“He told me that he was on a massive plane all by himself. I was under the impression it was a G5 or a G6.”She continued by explaining how Kolvet allegedly described the moment he arrived:“Finally, they land in Provo. The plane doors open and the first person he sees is Erica Kirk.”According to Owens, the reunion was deeply emotional. She said Kolvet told her he had broken down after seeing Erika, describing how he “collapsed into Erica's arms.”Owens said she initially understood the moment as a reaction to the shock and grief surrounding Charlie's death. However, she later became concerned when she heard a different account of Kolvet's travel arrangements.“I was also put immediately under the impression that it was Charlie's plane. So I was then surprised when Andrew's story down the line seemed to shift to me and it became that he was with his wife flying from Santa Barbara.”She said Kolvet had also told her that his wife asked whether she should fly to Utah. Owens interpreted that conversation as meaning they had travelled separately.Andrew Kolvet's flight details become the focus of Owens' allegationsOwens said she later raised the question during a meeting with Erika Kirk and Justin Strife, who she said had arranged the flights.“I asked them who flew on each plane on that day. And more specifically, I said, did Andrew fly with his wife?”According to Owens, Strife initially said Kolvet's wife was supposed to be on the plane but that he needed to confirm whether she boarded. Owens said he later messaged her to say the wife had travelled on the flight.She expected Erika to clarify the matter, but claimed the response never came.“But no, Erica blanked me. She did the Erica thing. The I, she stood there.”Owens argued that Erika should have remembered the alleged reunion if Kolvet's wife had been present. She also questioned why Erika would have waited for Kolvet's plane to arrive before travelling to the hospital after Charlie was shot.“I instantly felt they were lying, and now I believe that I have evidence that proves that I was correct and they were indeed lying.”Owens concluded that she believes Kolvet may have travelled alone on Charlie's plane. However, her account alone does not establish who boarded the aircraft or whether anyone deliberately gave false information.
